title: Encore · choose the visual world for the performance screen
question: The roll assigned Calling the Show. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every card keeps your pinned rule: a photographic room owns the screen, no game HUD.

options.label: Calling the Show
options.lineage: the stage manager's desk: prompt book, cue lights, house monitor, show report
options.thesis: The TV is the stage manager's desk: the real house on the monitor, your set run as cues, and a show report afterwards that only records what happened.
options.viewport: Full-bleed photographic audience as the house feed; one baseline cue strip along the foot with STANDBY → GO states in cue-light colour; a small running clock top-left; nothing boxed.
options.risk: Backstage jargon can read cold to a family on game night; the cue strip must stay to one line or it becomes the HUD you banned.

raised.raise: Nothing on the house is ever enclosed: cue text rides a baseline over the crowd, no boxes, rules or panels.
One pull changes everything: STANDBY → GO re-lights the whole house, instead of flipping a widget.
The labour beneath the spectacle is shown: the show report lists every measured signal behind every reaction.
The venue is a governing swatch: choosing Open Mic or Arena re-colours the house, the crowd and the MC's tone together, visibly.

options.label: House-Right Camera
options.lineage: the audience cutaways of a filmed comedy special
options.thesis: The TV behaves like the live director of a comedy special: wide room, reaction close-up, back to wide, cut on your laughs.
options.viewport: A cinematic wide of the room with shallow depth; reactions arrive as cuts to faces; a lower-third carries the set clock and nothing else.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most runs in this category land, a crowd film with lower-thirds; it wins on belief, not on surprise.

options.label: Meter Bridge
options.lineage: a VU-meter bridge across a recording desk
options.thesis: The room's reaction read as ballistic needles behind glass that lean into the red together on the punchline.
options.viewport: A row of real VU meters along the foot of the screen, the photographic house above them; every needle rests until the laugh, then the whole bridge leans right.
options.case: Fuses well: laughter level becomes a true physical reading performers already trust; loses on audience identification for families, who do not read meters.
options.risk: A desk of instruments can become a costume; the needles must obey real mass and damping or they read as a gauge widget.

options.label: Marquee Program
options.lineage: a desert strip sign shop's neon program drawing
options.thesis: Venues as a neon marquee: acts stacked as billed tenants, difficulty as the chase lamps, tonight's room behind the sign.
options.viewport: The venue sign fills the screen with your act as the top tenant and the arrow chase running at the chosen difficulty; the room is glimpsed behind it.
options.case: Holds audience identification: every performer knows the club marquee; loses product clarity on the performance screen, where the sign hides the room.
options.risk: Strong for the venue picker, wrong for the set itself; neon over a photographic crowd becomes decoration.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Bitmap text riding baselines over a black void, rank as depth.
options.viewport: One ivory line of bitmap text over a void with dust drifting behind it.
options.case: Performers and families do not identify with the demoscene, and a void cannot hold a real room.
options.kept: Nothing is ever enclosed by a rule or a box.
options.risk: Reads as a retro effect, not a venue.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: a silk cape transformed by one drawcord
options.thesis: A flat plane that one pull turns into ribs, gathers and volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle gathering into a pleated shell.
options.case: An object from fashion, not from the performer's world; it cannot carry a photographic crowd.
options.kept: One pull transforms the whole plane, never a widget.

options.label: Bosquet Vistas
options.thesis: Axial vistas, concealed green theatres, fountains waking in sequence.
options.viewport: A palace-terrace vista that breaks into secret theatres.
options.case: Beautiful, but neither performers nor families identify with a royal garden, and it says nothing about a reacting room.
options.kept: Show the labour beneath the spectacle.
options.risk: Decorative grandeur with no product truth.

options.label: Character Sheet
options.thesis: Four views, named swatches, hand-lettered rules in the leftover space.
options.viewport: A creature in four views over a busy tiled ground.
options.case: Illustrated and clashing: the opposite of the photographic realism you pinned.
options.kept: One swatch governs every region it controls.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A full-bleed crowd photo under a dark gradient with a mood meter, a timer and a transcript panel, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Crowd behind a scrim; meter top-left, timer top-right, transcript and tips in a panel at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AI-coach app by design.
